title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S is a smooth relative curve, and Ω is the line bundle of the formal 'fibre'. On the facing pages Ω also appears as Ω^{⊗2} and as Ω^1_{X/S}. One considers the completed symmetric algebra 𝒮 = Ŝ = Sym^∧(Ω) = ∏_{i≥0} Ω^{⊗i}. This is the structure sheaf of a formal line bundle (formal disc) over X with a marked section. Its augmentation ideal is J, with J^i/J^{i+1} = Ω^{⊗i}.

A 'connection' on Ŝ (relative to X/S) is a map C : Ŝ → Ŝ ⊗̂ Ω^1_{X/S}. It is a continuous derivation along X satisfying the Leibniz rule. It is determined by its value on a local generator ω0 of Ω: C(ω0) = Σ_{i≥0} ω0^i ⊗ ϖ_i, with ϖ_i local 1-forms (intrinsically ϖ_i ∈ Ω^1_{X/S} ⊗ Ω^{1-i}).

The Leibniz rule C(λω0) = λC(ω0) + ω0 dλ gives the expansion 1⊗λϖ0 + ω0⊗(λϖ1 + dλ) + ω0^2⊗λϖ2 + ⋯. Only the coefficient of degree 1 is affected by dλ. Hence:
- ϖ1 behaves like an ordinary connection form on Ω.
- ϖ0 and the ϖ_i for i ≥ 2 are tensorial.

Grothendieck then looks at the filtration. C maps J^i → J^{i-1} ⊗ Ω^1_{X/S}: the connection lowers the J-adic filtration by one, i.e. Griffiths transversality. Since d(λω) = λdω + ω dλ and ω dλ ∈ J⊗Ω^1, the term in dλ dies modulo J ⊗ Ω^1. So the induced graded maps gr: Ω^{⊗i} → Ω^{⊗(i-1)} ⊗ Ω^1_{X/S} are O-linear (the label over the arrow probably reads 'lin'). They are given by λω^i ↦ λ ω^{i-1}·ϖ0ω, up to a factor i.

The key invariant is ϖ0 ∈ Ω^{-1} ⊗ Ω^1_{X/S} = Hom(Ω, Ω^1_{X/S}), the Kodaira–Spencer-type map. This is the circled term. The line 'Ω → Ω^1_{X/S} = Ω' expresses the non-degeneracy condition that ϖ0 be an isomorphism, so that one may identify Ω = Ω^1_{X/S}. In modern terms this is the transversality (oper) condition: the flat formal P^1- (or formal-disc-) bundle with its section has nowhere-vanishing derivative.

Purpose: the next page changes the formal coordinate, ω̃0 = ω0/(1+Σα_iω0^i), to kill the higher coefficients ϖ_i for i ≥ 3. The resulting normal form C(ω0) = ϖ0 + ω0ϖ1 + ω0^2ϖ2 is the sl2 / PGL2 normal form, i.e. a projective connection. The obstruction there is (n+1)α_n = 0, so factorials and characteristic matter.

Together with the previous page (rigidity, and a pseudo-torsor under Γ(X, Ω^{⊗2})), the page sets up the dictionary: projective connections ↔ transverse connections on the formal disc bundle ↔ uniformizing data. The space of projective connections is an affine space (pseudo-torsor) under quadratic differentials.
errors: The formula on the graded pieces omits the factor i. The Leibniz rule gives C(λω^i) = ω^i⊗dλ + iλω^{i-1}C(ω), so the induced graded map Ω^{⊗i} → Ω^{⊗(i-1)}⊗Ω^1 is i·ϖ0, not ϖ0. This matters in positive or mixed characteristic, which the next page implicitly acknowledges through the conditions (n+1)α_n = 0.
ϖ_i is written as a section of Ω^1_{X/S}. Intrinsically it lies in Ω^1_{X/S} ⊗ Ω^{⊗(1-i)}; this is harmless once ω0 trivializes Ω.
The 'connection' C is only required to be a derivation (Leibniz) along X. Flatness is not discussed, but it is automatic for relative curves.

ideas.what: Encoding a projective structure on a curve as a connection (derivation along X) on the completed symmetric algebra Sym^∧(Ω), the formal disc bundle with a section, expanded in coefficients ϖ_i
ideas.modern_name: Flat connection on the formal disc bundle / Aut(O)-torsor (formal geometry, Harish-Chandra pairs); jet-bundle description of projective connections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gelfand–Kazhdan formal geometry (1971); Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s); Deligne (Équations différentielles, 1970) for projective connections via jets; Gunning (projective structures, 1960s)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such. Related themes appear in Grothendieck's crystalline/stratification formalism (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1968).

ideas.what: Transversality: the connection lowers the J-adic filtration by one, the graded maps are O-linear, and the leading coefficient ϖ0 ∈ Hom(Ω, Ω^1_{X/S}) must be an isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Griffiths transversality / oper (non-degeneracy) condition; Kodaira–Spencer map of the section

ideas.what: Gauge reduction by change of formal coordinate to the quadratic (sl2) normal form ϖ0 + ω0ϖ1 + ω0^2ϖ2, carried out on the next page
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld–Sokolov gauge / reduction of an Aut(O)-oper to a PGL2-oper; projective connection

ideas.what: Leibniz-rule bookkeeping showing that only ϖ1 transforms affinely (as a connection form on Ω) while the other ϖ_i are tensorial

missed.claim: Grothendieck anticipates the 'oper' viewpoint on projective structures. A projective connection is treated as a flat connection on the formal neighbourhood of a section of a formal line bundle, Sym^∧(Ω), satisfying a transversality condition (ϖ0 : Ω ≅ Ω^1_{X/S}). It is then reduced to an sl2 normal form by formal coordinate changes, with explicit attention to integrality ((n+1)α_n = 0) over a general base S. This is essentially the Beilinson–Drinfeld / Drinfeld–Sokolov picture, with an arithmetic (relative, any base) flavour.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical rather than new mathematics: it documents an independent, undated formulation of opers in relative and possibly mixed-characteristic settings. That setting is relevant to the current study of dormant opers and p-adic uniformization (Mochizuki), where the factorial obstructions visible here are central.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations themselves are routine (Leibniz expansion, filtration, leading term). The framework, however — transverse connections on Sym^∧(Ω) over a general base, aimed at uniformization and normalized to PGL2 form — is a recognizably oper-like approach that is not recorded in Grothendieck's published work. The page is undated, so priority claims are impossible.
transcription_corrections: The label over the arrow 'Ω^i --h_i[?]--> Ω^{i-1}⊗Ω^1_{X/S}' most likely reads 'lin' (linéaire), signalling that the graded map is O-linear.
In 'd(λω) = λdω + [ω dλ struck] nul mod J⊗Ω^1_{X/S}', the words are 'nul mod': the dλ-term vanishes modulo J⊗Ω^1.
'C(ω) = ϖ0 ω + [?] ≥1' probably reads 'C(ω) = ϖ0ω + (termes de degré) ≥ 1', with ϖ0 ∈ Ω^1_{X/S}⊗Ω^{-1} written below it.
The circled expression is 'λω^i ϖ0', the leading term of the graded map.
The final lines 'Conn*' and 'Ŝ* = L[?]' are barely legible; the second may be 'Ŝ* = L'.
